title: C124 — Low brake fluid warning indicator switch connector
introduction:
I use this reference to connect the low brake fluid warning switch’s connector drawing with its wiring information. Start with the identification table, find the cavity labels in the drawing, then follow the matching rows across the pin-assignment table. The housing gets you to the right neighborhood; the cavity and circuit labels give you the address.

The function column separates the switch circuit from the ground connection. The pigtail table then provides a separate lookup for the listed service assembly and its engineering shell. Housing identity, circuit identity and service-part identity answer different questions, so I check each in its own column.

This page teaches identification and table reading. Access, electrical testing and connector replacement require their matching service information. The drawing’s physical viewing direction and the conventions behind Gauge, Size and Used are unspecified here; they are not a basis for probing or choosing replacement wire.

edits.why: I use the broad latch outline above the vertically stacked cavity labels to orient the drawing on the page. Match each drawn cavity label to the Cavity column, then use the adjoining Fpn and Harness Id fields to check the reference identity. These landmarks describe the illustration; they do not establish whether a physical connector is being viewed from its terminal side or wire side.

edits.text: Read the cavity and circuit assignments
edits.why: Read across a single cavity row to keep its circuit identifier, color code, gauge entry, function and terminal part number together. The switch function and the left-front fender ground function describe different electrical roles. A ground destination label identifies the connection’s purpose, but does not show its physical access route or prove that the connection is sound.

edits.text: Identify the listed pigtail service assembly
edits.why: The Number field connects this entry to the Kit List above. Service Part identifies the listed pigtail assembly, while Engineering Shell lets you compare its housing identity with the connector information. Keep the pigtail’s gauge and material entries separate from the vehicle circuit rows; this lookup does not teach wire selection, splicing or installation.
